sources.note: C4 accelerates diffusion language model decoding with two separate gates: one that decides when the whole sequence may stop, by checking that the extracted answer span is both confident and unchanged for several steps, and one that decides which token positions a step may commit, by committing only a boundary-anchored run and confirming deferred positions one step later.
sources.title: Commit Locally, Exit Globally: Coordinating Adaptive Sampling and Early Exit in Diffusion Language Models

sources.note: Assigns a per-prompt sampling budget for best-of-N test-time scaling with a hand-written two-stage fuzzy controller over nine prompt- and model-side signals, trading 1.4-14.5% fewer samples for accuracy changes between -1.8 and +0.5 points against a selector-matched fixed N = 8 baseline.
sources.title: Interpretable Adaptive Sampling for LLM Test-Time Scaling

sources.note: Trains a 1.5B reasoning model to emit one of three mode tokens (NoThink, Short, Long) as the very first token of its response and to reason under that mode's budget, learned end-to-end inside GRPO with no separate router.
sources.title: Learning When to Think: Adaptive Reasoning for Test-Time Compute Allocation

sources.note: An empirical study showing reasoning LLMs overthink easy questions and underthink hard ones, and that preferring shorter outputs via SimPO can cut generation length 30-60% with little accuracy loss.
sources.title: Between Underthinking and Overthinking: An Empirical Study of Reasoning Length and correctness in LLMs

sources.note: AutoThink uses a three-stage RL curriculum with stage-wise reward shaping to teach R1-style distilled models to decide per problem whether to emit an explicit reasoning chain at all.
sources.title: Learning When to Think: Shaping Adaptive Reasoning in R1-Style Models via Multi-Stage RL

sources.note: ImgCoT compresses a long chain of thought into a small set of latent tokens by training the autoencoder to reconstruct an image of the rendered CoT rather than its text.
sources.title: ImgCoT: Compressing Long Chain of Thought into Compact Visual Tokens for Efficient Reasoning of Large Language Model

sources.note: ARM trains a model to pick among four reasoning formats (Direct Answer, Short CoT, Code, Long CoT) per task using Ada-GRPO, cutting average tokens by about 30% at roughly unchanged accuracy.
sources.title: ARM: Adaptive Reasoning Model

sources.note: Under a fixed sampling-compute budget, synthetic reasoning data generated by sampling many solutions from a smaller, weaker model trains better reasoners than fewer solutions from a larger, stronger one.
sources.title: Smaller, Weaker, Yet Better: Training LLM Reasoners via Compute-Optimal Sampling

sources.note: Shows diffusion LLMs implicitly contain a mixture of semi-autoregressive generation experts and introduces a training-free method that majority-votes across multiple block generation schedules to substantially boost accuracy.
sources.title: TEST-TIME SCALING IN DIFFUSION LLMS VIA HIDDEN SEMI-AUTOREGRESSIVE EXPERTS

sources.note: DC-CoT is a benchmark that isolates the effect of data augmentation, data selection and data mixing on chain-of-thought distillation into smaller student models, across teacher models, student models and reasoning domains.
sources.title: The Quest for Efficient Reasoning: A Data-Centric Benchmark to CoT Distillation

sources.note: T1 is a two-stage test-time-scaling framework for small language models that filters candidate responses with external tools before a small-model verifier makes the final judgment, offloading memorization-heavy checks to the tools.
sources.title: T1: Tool-integrated Verification for Test-time Compute Scaling in Small Language Models

sources.note: Routes queries between a thinking and a non-thinking model with a threshold that is adjusted online by a betting supermartingale, so the accumulated statistical evidence certifies at any stopping time that the accuracy given up stays under a user-specified tolerance.
sources.title: Anytime Safe PAC Efficient Reasoning

sources.note: ATTS uses conformal prediction to asynchronously coordinate multi-dimensional test-time scaling, cutting synchronization overhead between draft and target models during LLM inference.
sources.title: ATTS: Asynchronous Test-Time Scaling via Conformal Prediction

sources.note: ShorterBetter takes the length of the shortest correct response in a sampled group as a per-problem target and rewards the model for matching it, cutting output length by 50%-80% on DeepSeek-Distill-Qwen-1.5B/7B.
sources.title: ShorterBetter: Guiding Reasoning Models to Find Optimal Inference Length for Efficient Reasoning

sources.note: Shows cross-entropy fine-tuning can hurt pass@N test-time performance via overconfidence, and proposes a confidence-limiting training loss that better aligns training with pass@N search.
sources.title: Rethinking Fine-Tuning when Scaling Test-Time Compute: Limiting Confidence Improves Mathematical Reasoning

sources.note: Analyses the scaling behaviour of self-consistency sampling as mode estimation, derives power-law error decay in the number of samples, and introduces Blend-ASC, a hyperparameter-free scheme that reallocates a fixed sample budget across questions.
sources.title: Optimal Self-Consistency for Efficient Reasoning with Large Language Models

instructions:
Revise the wiki definition for 'MATH'.

It was written against fewer sources than the archive now holds. The sources below are all of them, including the ones that have arrived since.

This is the definition as it stands:

    The MATH competition-mathematics dataset, used in the archive both directly (e.g. 'Between Underthinking and Overthinking' evaluates on MATH and GSM8K to show reasoning models overthink easy questions and underthink hard ones) and via its curated 500-problem subset MATH-500/MATH500 used by most other archived test-time-compute papers. Note: the wiki tracks this dataset family under three separate, unmerged spellings.

**Keep what still holds.** Change it where a later source contradicts it, narrows it, or shows the term being used in a way the old text does not cover — and say so plainly rather than hedging the original into something vaguer. If the new sources change nothing, return it unchanged; that is a real answer and it records that somebody checked.

A definition that enumerates its sources by name is the one most likely to be quietly wrong now. Prefer stating what the term means to counting where it appears.

Rules:
- Write in en.
- Ground every statement in the supplied material. If something is not stated,
  leave the field empty rather than inferring it.
- No marketing language. Prefer the specific number over the adjective.
- Return one JSON object matching the schema exactly. No prose around it.

result.definition: The 12,500-problem competition-mathematics dataset of Hendrycks et al., used in this archive far more often as a training corpus and a probe set than as a test set -- reinforcement-learning runs train on its lighteval split, and steering and probing work samples a few hundred problems from it to collect hidden states. Where it appears as an evaluation it is usually the held-out Hendrycks-MATH set rather than the full corpus. Sources are inconsistent about the name: 'MATH' sometimes denotes this dataset and sometimes a composite maths benchmark a paper assembled from MATH500 and AIME sets, so a number attributed to 'MATH' needs its source checked.
